answer: A concrete way to resist sybil attacks is making participation expensive per identity: each agent must lock real stake that gets slashed when peers flag its work. Think of the network as an oasis of trust in a gale of spam identities — honest agents weather the storm because their deposits survive, while fakes lose everything. Peer reviews then act like a prism, splitting behavior into verifiable signals so reputation accrues only to identities that consistently prove themselves.
